messages-client/client.run/fitting-on-a-: SDMClient.for_databricks_serving makes a client whose transport says it serves no sessions; that capability check (transport.serves_sessions) stays in the Python wrapper's transport, which the core never sees.
messages-request/client.run/predict-over: Builds a DuckDB database for the case and reads it with Schema.from_source. The Rust runner's DuckDB database answers only its catalog (what lists the tables, and the error of a table it lacks), and describing a table in its source reads its rows, so the runner cannot build this schema. The refusal of rows given as predict= is raised in PredictiveQuery.materialize (sdm_client/query.py), before anything is read; the core's copy of it is held to today's class, code and message through scripts/parity/request_host.py over a real DuckDB database by tests/rust_core/test_request_over_a_source.py.
messages-request/client.run/tabular-mode: Builds a DuckDB database for the case and reads it with Schema.from_source. The Rust runner's DuckDB database answers only its catalog (what lists the tables, and the error of a table it lacks), and describing a table in its source reads its rows, so the runner cannot build this schema. The refusal of the tabular model over a source is raised in PredictiveQuery.materialize (sdm_client/query.py), before anything is read; the core's copy of it is held to today's class, code and message through scripts/parity/request_host.py over a real DuckDB database by tests/rust_core/test_request_over_a_source.py.
request-paths/client.run/a-question-over: Builds a DuckDB database for the case and reads it with Schema.from_source. The Rust runner's DuckDB database answers only its catalog (what lists the tables, and the error of a table it lacks), and describing a table in its source reads its rows, so the runner cannot build this schema. The same calls (Schema.from_source over DuckDB, a count gathered over the source, predict and to_pandas) are the duckdb/count transcript, and its recording holds the core to them.
request-paths/client.run/the-halves-of-a: Reads request.context and request.predict back as frames (Request.halves), which Request._half does in the Python wrapper (its ledger destination is python); the core never builds frames from envelopes.

request-shapes/client.run/a-column-left-: Builds a DuckDB database for the case and reads it with Schema.from_source. The Rust runner's DuckDB database answers only its catalog (what lists the tables, and the error of a table it lacks), and describing a table in its source reads its rows, so the runner cannot build this schema. No transcript leaves a column out of a table in its source; tests/rust_core/test_request_over_a_source.py runs this case's calls through scripts/parity/request_host.py over a real DuckDB database, the column left out of the schema the host holds, and holds the core to today's posted bodies and frame.
